seo.title: How to Build a Portfolio with Astro | Developer Portfolio Guide
seo.description: Build a fast, beautiful developer portfolio with Astro featuring project showcases, a blog section, and perfect Lighthouse scores.

introduction: Your portfolio is your most important marketing tool as a developer or designer. Astro is the perfect framework for portfolios because it ships zero JavaScript by default, giving you a 100/100 Lighthouse score without any optimization work. You can still use React, Vue, or Svelte components where you need interactivity. This guide builds a complete portfolio with project showcases, an about page, a contact form, and smooth view transitions.

prerequisites.name: Node.js 20+
prerequisites.description: Required to run Astro and its build tools.

prerequisites.name: Basic HTML and CSS
prerequisites.description: Astro components use HTML-like syntax with scoped styles, so HTML and CSS knowledge is essential.

prerequisites.name: Project Screenshots or Mockups
prerequisites.description: Prepare images or screenshots of 3-5 projects you want to showcase in your portfolio.

steps.title: Create the Astro Project with Tailwind CSS
steps.description: Scaffold a minimal Astro project and add Tailwind CSS for styling. Unlike the blog template, start with the minimal template so you control the entire structure. Add the sitemap integration for SEO and the image integration for automatic optimization.

code_snippet.code:
npm create astro@latest my-portfolio -- --template minimal
cd my-portfolio
npx astro add tailwind
npx astro add sitemap
npm install

tips: The minimal template gives you a clean slate without any preset pages or components.
Set your site URL in astro.config.mjs immediately — it is needed for sitemap generation and canonical URLs.

steps.title: Create the Base Layout with Navigation
steps.description: Build a reusable layout component with a responsive navigation bar, SEO meta tags, and a footer. Astro layouts use slots to wrap page content, similar to React children. The layout includes Open Graph tags for social sharing and a mobile-friendly hamburger menu.

code_snippet.code:
--- // src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro interface Props { title: string; description: string; image?: string; } const { title, description, image = "/og-image.jpg" } = Astro.props; const canonicalUrl = new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site); --- {title}
YourName
  • Projects
  • About
  • Contact

© {new Date().getFullYear()} YourName. All rights reserved.

tips: Use backdrop-blur-sm on the navbar for a frosted glass effect that keeps content readable underneath.
Add View Transitions later with a single component import for smooth page navigation.

steps.title: Define a Project Content Collection
steps.description: Create a content collection for your portfolio projects with a typed schema. Each project has a title, description, tech stack, links, images, and display order. Content collections give you type safety and build-time validation for all your project data.
tips: Use the 'featured' flag to highlight your best 2-3 projects on the homepage.
The 'order' field lets you control project display order without renaming files.

steps.title: Build the Homepage with Hero and Project Grid
steps.description: Create the homepage with a hero section introducing yourself and a grid of featured projects. The hero section should communicate who you are, what you do, and include a call-to-action. The project grid uses your content collection to display project cards with hover effects.

code_snippet.code:
--- // src/pages/index.astro import BaseLayout from "../layouts/BaseLayout.astro"; import { getCollection } from "astro:content"; import { Image } from "astro:assets"; const projects = (await getCollection("projects")) .sort((a, b) => a.data.order - b.data.order); const featured = projects.filter((p) => p.data.featured); ---

steps.title: Create Individual Project Pages
steps.description: Build detail pages for each project using Astro's dynamic routing. Each page shows the full project description, tech stack, screenshots, and links to the live site and source code. Use getStaticPaths to generate a page for every project in your collection at build time.
tips: Write detailed case studies in the Markdown body — explain the problem, your approach, and the results.
Add before/after screenshots or performance comparisons to demonstrate impact.

steps.title: Add View Transitions for Smooth Navigation
steps.description: Enable Astro's built-in View Transitions API for smooth, app-like page navigation without a JavaScript framework. Pages morph between each other with crossfade animations, and you can add per-element transitions for project images that expand from the grid to the detail page.
tips: Use the same transition:name on elements across pages to create morphing animations between them.
View Transitions work in Chrome, Edge, and Safari — Firefox falls back to standard navigation gracefully.

steps.title: Deploy to Vercel or Netlify
steps.description: Deploy your portfolio to a global CDN for near-instant page loads worldwide. Astro's static output works on any hosting platform. Connect your custom domain and set up automatic deployments from your Git repository so every push updates your live site.

code_snippet.code:
# Build and verify locally
npm run build
npm run preview

# Deploy to Vercel
npx astro add vercel
npx vercel --prod

# Or deploy to Netlify
npx astro add netlify
npx netlify deploy --prod --dir=dist

tips: Set up a custom domain — yourname.dev or yourname.com — for a professional impression.
Add Plausible or Fathom analytics to track which projects get the most views without compromising visitor privacy.
Run a Lighthouse audit after deploying — Astro portfolios should score 95+ across all categories.
